title: Messel Pit, Germany: an Eocene ecosystem
summary: Messel, near Darmstadt in Hesse, was a crater lake about 300 m deep that formed roughly 48 million years ago when magma met groundwater in steam explosions, in a tropical climate with dense jungle around it. Its oil shale preserved over 1000 species of plants and animals, including complete mammal skeletons, crocodiles, fish, birds and bats, with feathers, skin and hair.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO gives 47–48 million years for the middle Eocene record; Senckenberg says about 48 million years.

as_recorded.value: a detailed geological record of middle Eocene age, dating from 47-48 million years ago

where.modern_name: Messel Pit, Messel, District of Darmstadt-Dieburg, Hesse, Germany
where.historical_name: Messel maar lake, Eocene Europe (no polity)

importance.justification: The richest known site for the Eocene living environment and early mammal evolution, with exceptional soft-tissue preservation.
